page: Amazon Web Services r8id.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning features 256 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation designed for memory-bound computational tasks.

Storage and connectivity specifications include 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system does not incorporate discrete GPU hardware, relying instead on integrated CPU instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), AVX-512 vector acceleration (including BF16 and VNNI), and hardware-level cryptographic extensions like VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong computational throughput, with Geekbench results of 2194.0 single-core and 17990.0 multi-core, as well as a PassMark CPU score of 51704.46. The platform demonstrates top-quartile performance in data compression pipelines, static web serving at 58.85 GB/sec, and small model language inference. Larger parameter model generation benchmarks reflect execution tradeoffs on unaccelerated CPU silicon. The instance suits workloads such as in-memory databases, Redis clusters, analytics, and applications requiring high-speed local scratch disk space.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.8xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based instance featuring an Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz with 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and a 480 MB L3 cache. It delivers 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory alongside 1900 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage and 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The CPU integrates Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions, supporting accelerated vector and tensor calculations without a dedicated GPU. Benchmark profiles demonstrate solid single-thread and multithread processing alongside upper-tier compression and image processing throughput, while PassMark database operations and Redis SET performance reach median tier stability. Given the 8 GB per vCPU allocation and fast local NVMe storage, this instance is suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, high-throughput web serving, and analytical data processing pipelines requiring rapid temporary disk access.
